brief: The FOMC unanimously raised the fed funds rate 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, with the dot plot pointing to one more 2026 hike (median 4.00%-4.25%) and rates unchanged through 2027. Chair Warsh was hawkish, calling the move 'removing a dose of policy accommodation,' and 16 of 18 officials pencilled in at least one more hike. Markets read guidance as more hawkish than expected: futures now price an 89% probability of a December hike, versus 93-94% pre-meeting odds for the September move itself. Syz frames the hike as a credibility exercise following 2025 easing amid a fresh energy shock, not the start of a long tightening cycle, expecting one or two more hikes (a third possible in early 2027) that would fully unwind last year's easing. Because August retail sales rebounded 1.2% and growth stays solid, Syz argues earnings impact is limited. Historically the S&P falls ~2% in the three months after a hike before gaining ~9% over the next year. Syz stays neutral on the dollar, short duration on Treasuries (bear flattener), keeps gold as a strategic hedge despite the textbook headwind, and favours equities (neutral) over fixed income (underweight), pairing mega-cap tech with cyclicals if oil/inflation stay sticky.
